In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the internalist–externalism debate has been too narrowly construed in contemporary epistemological discussions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
scientific justification is best understood as a form of objective justification that is both internally and externally directed.
the internalist–externalism debate in epistemology is not a debate that can be applied directly to scientific contexts.

the debate between internalists, who think that justification is a relation between a person and a belief, and externalists, who think justification is a relation among a person’s beliefs, is not a useful way of thinking about scientific justification.
The main takeaway from our work is that

an objective approach to evidence can be useful in clarifying the nature of scientific justification, but that it also highlights the need for more work on how the nature of justification in science relates to the nature of justification for individual beliefs.
objective accounts of scientific inquiry, such as Mayo’s, have the potential to shed light on the internalist–externalism debate in epistemology.
